6\. New chat inputs skip shared validation 📘 Rule violation ≡ Correctness 
validate_new_chat_arguments validates a raw mapping with local type, length, and mode checks
instead of using the shared input-validation module and a Pydantic model. Both the chat tool and the
controller call this helper, so new creation fields follow a separate validation path at those
boundaries.
Agent Prompt ``` ## Issue description New chat creation fields are validated locally instead of through the shared Pydantic-based validation module. ## Fix Focus Areas - tldw_chatbook/Chat/console_agent_bridge.py[11381-11413] - tldw_chatbook/Utils/input_validation.py[1-60] ## Recommended Fix Define a typed, constrained chat-creation model in the shared module and use its validated values at both chat-creation boundaries. ``` ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools

The tool and controller now share the strict Pydantic creation boundary in Utils/input_validation.py. It preserves non-coercion, literal prompt/instruction bytes, defaults, length checks and stable ValueError categories; model-supplied authority fields still cannot grant access. Complete validation/integration/note owners passed194 cases at their recorded source. 1\. Chat approval can stall the console 📘 Rule violation ➹ Performance 
ConsoleChatStartCoordinator.accept calls the synchronous accept_chat_start database operation
directly from an async submission path. When the admission transaction waits on SQLite or takes time
to complete, it blocks the event loop that handles the console; nearby database work uses
run_owned_db_call to run off-thread.
Agent Prompt ``` ## Issue description Chat-start acceptance runs synchronous database admission on the async console path. ## Fix Focus Areas - tldw_chatbook/Chat/console_chat_start.py[463-480] - tldw_chatbook/DB/base_db.py[64-89] ## Recommended Fix Run admission through the owned database worker while preserving the final source checks and single-claim ownership cutoff across the handoff. ``` ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools
[Dismiss ↗](https://app.qodo.ai/findings/a73846d0-a4cd-43e5-93d8-8d4987ee687d?action=dismiss&origin=git) | [View ↗](https://app.qodo.ai/findings/a73846d0-a4cd-43e5-93d8-8d4987ee687d)

SQLite writer contention now refuses immediately using the operation-owned acceptance connection with scoped busy_timeout=0, restored in finally. Actual file-lock controls verify refusal and event-loop progress. Acceptance retains the no-await source/target cutoff; simply moving it off-thread would let authority change after the last guard. Native conversation commit is separately owned, shielded and drained off-thread. Cold connection opening and FULL fsync remain synchronous; this does not claim all I/O latency is bounded. Publication: 27a7aca284394852cb37a80deb6db55ba5319be7; connection/restore/cancellation evidence and this remaining limit are recorded in the Task4 report.

4\. Saved notes mislabel agent messages 🐞 Bug ≡ Correctness 
build_transcript_note() prefixes every user-role message with User without inspecting the new
agent_chat_start or untrusted origin. When a transcript includes an agent handoff or an
unverified handoff, its saved note presents that message as human-authored despite the Console
displaying a distinct speaker label.
Agent Prompt ``` ## Issue description Transcript notes label newly distinguished agent and unverified handoffs as ordinary user messages. ## Fix Focus Areas - tldw_chatbook/Chat/console_roleplay_identity.py[264-272] - tldw_chatbook/Chat/console_chat_controller.py[22246-22261] ## Recommended Fix Use the message origin when choosing each exported note line's speaker label, retaining the agent-handoff and unverified-handoff distinctions. ``` ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools

Saved transcript notes now label machine-origin requests Agent handoff and untrusted requests Unverified handoff. Ordinary human User and assistant labels, span selection and provenance remain intact. Original note owners and explicit provenance controls passed. 5\. A failed background start blocks the chat's automatic work until restart 🐞 Bug ☼ Reliability 
In ConsoleChatStartCoordinator._run, cleanup calls complete_chat_start only when
item.receipted is true and abort_chat_start only when item.accepted is false, so an attempt
that was accepted but never got a receipt is never settled in the ledger. This happens when
commit_durable_turn raises after accept() (including ContinuationAdmissionRefused, where the
transaction is known to have rolled back) or when confirm_receipt fails. The row then stays
accepted, its committed generation stays charged to the shared allowance, and _target_active
refuses every later wake or chat start for that conversation until recover() runs under a new
runtime owner.
Agent Prompt ``` ## Issue description When a chat start is accepted in the ledger (`accept_chat_start`) but the durable turn commit fails or `confirm_receipt` is never reached, `_run` leaves the `automatic_chat_start_attempts` row in state `accepted`. That row blocks every later wake or start for the conversation (`_target_active`) and keeps the generation charged until a process restart under a new owner. ## Fix Focus Areas - tldw_chatbook/Chat/console_chat_start.py[364-408] - tldw_chatbook/DB/automatic_work.py[857-891] - tldw_chatbook/Chat/console_chat_controller.py[12773-12839] ## Recommended Fix Add a ledger transition for accepted-but-unreceipted attempts, for example `mark_chat_start_review_required(attempt_id, owner_id)`. It should move `accepted` to `review_required`, and it can pause the allowance root with `review_required`/`interrupted_work`. Call it from `_run`'s finally block when `item.accepted and not item.receipted`. Where the controller knows the commit rolled back (e.g. `ContinuationAdmissionRefused`), let the coordinator refund the reservation, either by setting a flag on the authorization or by adding a `revert_accepted_chat_start` operation. Add a test that makes `commit_durable_turn` raise after `accept()` and checks that the conversation can be woken or started again. ``` ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools
[Dismiss ↗](https://app.qodo.ai/findings/1f68c117-3ae2-45e3-a0c5-64a4e8834414?action=dismiss&origin=git) | [View ↗](https://app.qodo.ai/findings/1f68c117-3ae2-45e3-a0c5-64a4e8834414)

Accepted, unreceipted work now settles to the existing review_required ledger state and atomically pauses its canonical shared allowance. It remains charged, including a conversation-side rollback after ledger acceptance: refunding an already accepted attempt would violate ADR-219 and could enable replay. Failed durable settlement retains an owner-fenced runtime restriction; replacement-owner recovery is preserved. Physical native commit work drains before capacity release or uncertain settlement. Real ledger, cancellation and replacement-owner overlap controls passed, with exact evidence in Task4. Publication: 27a7aca284394852cb37a80deb6db55ba5319be7.

2\. A failed restriction strands chat-start capacity 🐞 Bug ☼ Reliability 
ConsoleChatStartCoordinator._run calls _restrict_chat_start outside a protective try at the
start of its cleanup block. If restriction registration raises, cleanup exits before draining owned
workers, resolving the outcome, or releasing the automatic-work capacity claim.
Agent Prompt ``` ## Issue description Restriction registration can raise before chat-start cleanup reaches worker draining, outcome resolution, and capacity release. ## Fix Focus Areas - tldw_chatbook/Chat/console_chat_start.py[424-597] - tldw_chatbook/DB/automatic_work.py[66-85] ## Recommended Fix Protect restriction registration so its failure cannot bypass the remaining cleanup. Preserve the conservative admission restriction where possible, and ensure owned workers are drained and the exact capacity claim is released even when registration fails. ``` ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools
[Dismiss ↗](https://app.qodo.ai/findings/3d1df7df-2f52-4029-b657-6d7e198f623d?action=dismiss&origin=git) | [View ↗](https://app.qodo.ai/findings/3d1df7df-2f52-4029-b657-6d7e198f623d)

Both cleanup registration sites now use a guarded helper, while both physical commit/provider owners drain before final cleanup and captured-token release. Nested cleanup preserves outcome fallback and replacement ownership through publication/abandonment/run-state errors. The correction also captures the canonical store identity before authority and retains same-registry denial when ordinary registration repeatedly fails and durable settlement cannot commit. The recorded initial 61-case phase and separate 27-case correction include actual native exit, repeated cancellation, alias-handle refusal and replacement-token controls. Published at 06cfe2f6a30236dcd8f81893ebf49bc3d0b78036; independent scoped approval and exact source-specific receipts: https://github.com/rmusser01/tldw_chatbook/blob/06cfe2f6a30236dcd8f81893ebf49bc3d0b78036/Docs/superpowers/qa/2026-10-04-console-pr2995-latest-dev-integration/review-follow-up.

3\. One failed chat-start setup halts all automatic agent work 🐞 Bug ☼ Reliability 
When _prepare fails with something other than AutomaticWorkRefused (for example, SQLite reports
the database is locked), item.context is still None. The _run cleanup then calls
_restrict_chat_start(chain_id=None) and tries abort_chat_start, but that raises
ValueError("unknown chat start attempt") because the attempt row was never written. The `except
BaseException` handler re-adds the None-chain restriction and never clears it.
_check_unconfirmed_starts treats a None member as matching every chain, so every later
_check_admission call by the current runtime owner in that database (wakes, chat starts, reserves,
automatic calls in every conversation) is refused with settlement_unconfirmed. This lasts until a
different owner runs recover(), in practice an app restart.
Agent Prompt ``` ## Issue description If `_prepare` fails with a non-refusal exception before the attempt row is committed, `_run` records a chain-less restriction (`chain_id=None`). `abort_chat_start` then raises `ValueError("unknown chat start attempt")`, and the settlement `except BaseException` keeps the None restriction. `_check_unconfirmed_starts` treats a None member as matching every chain, so all automatic admission for the current runtime owner is refused until restart. ## Fix Focus Areas - tldw_chatbook/Chat/console_chat_start.py[498-547] - tldw_chatbook/DB/automatic_work.py[93-113] - tldw_chatbook/DB/automatic_work.py[913-934] ## Recommended Fix Make a missing attempt row a confirmed "nothing to settle" result. For example, have `abort_chat_start` return a distinct value (or raise a dedicated exception) when the row does not exist inside its transaction. In `_run`, treat that result like a successful refund and call `_clear_chat_start_restriction`. Also consider scoping a None-chain restriction to the source chain's allowance root, which can be resolved from `source_run_id`, so that one uncertain preparation cannot block unrelated conversations. Add a test where `prepare_chat_start` raises `sqlite3.OperationalError` and check that later wakes in other conversations are still admitted. ``` ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools
[Dismiss ↗](https://app.qodo.ai/findings/d3ef0cd5-e6e8-4913-8a2a-d30973442ee7?action=dismiss&origin=git) | [View ↗](https://app.qodo.ai/findings/d3ef0cd5-e6e8-4913-8a2a-d30973442ee7)

Added a private absence predicate using the existing FULL/BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction: it requires a present matching durable runtime owner, queries the exact attempt, and returns positive only after successful transaction exit. Cleanup invokes it only for unaccepted/unreceipted/context-unavailable work after all physical owners drain. Confirmed absence clears only that attempt and captured owner restriction; query/begin/commit/policy-restoration failure remains conservative. Prepared and accepted commit-then-raise controls preserve their distinct refund/charged-review behavior. Strict public abort semantics are unchanged. Published at 06cfe2f6a30236dcd8f81893ebf49bc3d0b78036; real SQLite controls and independent review: https://github.com/rmusser01/tldw_chatbook/blob/06cfe2f6a30236dcd8f81893ebf49bc3d0b78036/Docs/superpowers/qa/2026-10-04-console-pr2995-latest-dev-integration/review-follow-up.

3\. Restored chat starts can lose authority 🐞 Bug ≡ Correctness 
The new agent_chat_start_attempt_id checkpoint field records an AgentRuns attempt, but recovery
still allows the Chachanotes database to be restored without the AgentRuns database that owns that
attempt. When a backup contains an accepted chat start, restoring only Chachanotes leaves its
checkpoint intact while the attempt required to authorize continued automatic work is absent.
Agent Prompt ``` ## Issue description An accepted chat-start checkpoint in Chachanotes can be restored without its authoritative attempt in AgentRuns, leaving a receipt that cannot authorize continued work. ## Fix Focus Areas - tldw_chatbook/DB/migrations/chachanotes_v76_to_v77_agent_chat_starts.sql[21-33] - tldw_chatbook/DB/recovery_core.py[500-516] - tldw_chatbook/DB/recovery_operations.py[1299-1308] ## Recommended Fix Make backup and restore selection or validation require a matching AgentRuns database whenever Chachanotes contains agent-chat-start checkpoints. Reject incomplete restore sets rather than leaving dangling accepted receipts, and add a test for a Chachanotes-only restore selection. ``` ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools
[Dismiss ↗](https://app.qodo.ai/findings/75d0cc3d-b86d-4278-9919-275aa482c282?action=dismiss&origin=git) | [View ↗](https://app.qodo.ai/findings/75d0cc3d-b86d-4278-9919-275aa482c282)

1\. Two existing test modules crash at setup 🐞 Bug ≡ Correctness 
InterruptRoundHost.__init__ changed from (self, seams) to a keyword-only signature with about
115 required getter arguments. Tests/Chat/test_console_decision_clock.py (5 call sites) and
Tests/UI/test_buddy_speech.py (setup()) still call InterruptRoundHost(seams) directly and were
not updated in this PR, so every test in those modules fails with TypeError before any test logic
runs.
Agent Prompt ``` ## Issue description `InterruptRoundHost` now needs keyword-only getter arguments. Two test modules still construct it as `InterruptRoundHost(seams)` and fail with `TypeError`. ## Fix Focus Areas - Tests/Chat/test_console_decision_clock.py[8-25] - Tests/UI/test_buddy_speech.py[11-49] - Tests/Chat/console_interrupt_test_bindings.py[8-20] ## Recommended Fix In both files, import `make_interrupt_host as InterruptRoundHost` from `Tests.Chat.console_interrupt_test_bindings`, as `test_console_interrupt_rounds.py` already does. Make sure the fakes they pass (`FakeSeamsFull`, and `SimpleNamespace(store=store)` in buddy speech) provide every attribute the binding helper reads. Alternatively, add a `from_seams` classmethod to `InterruptRoundHost` and use it. ``` ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools

4\. Interrupt host wiring hard to maintain 🐞 Bug ⚙ Maintainability 
The new InterruptRoundHost constructor takes about 115 getter callables, including module globals
such as read_global_Any, read_global_Mapping, read_global_os, read_global_time and
read_global_logger. Each is stored as its own attribute, and the controller has to pass a matching
lambda for each one. Any new controller attribute or module global that the host uses means editing
the constructor signature, the attribute list, the production lambda block in
ConsoleChatController and the test binding helper together. Missing any of these fails only at
construction time, or with an AttributeError on the code path that uses the new getter.
Agent Prompt ``` ## Issue description `InterruptRoundHost.__init__` takes about 115 keyword getter callables, including ones that only return module globals (`Any`, `os`, `time`, `logger`). This creates a wide interface that has to be kept in sync by hand across several files. ## Fix Focus Areas - tldw_chatbook/Chat/console_interrupt_rounds.py[236-650] - tldw_chatbook/Chat/console_chat_controller.py[4270-4299] - Tests/Chat/console_interrupt_test_bindings.py[8-20] ## Recommended Fix Use module globals directly inside `console_interrupt_rounds.py` instead of injecting `read_global_*` getters. Group the controller-facing dependencies into a typed `Protocol` (or a small dataclass of the callables actually needed) and pass one object. That keeps the explicit-dependency goal while restoring a single-argument constructor that existing callers and tests can use. ``` ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools
